title: Meta’s AI agent Muse is mixing up conversations and could be exposing private data, report says
lede: Meta employees say its Muse agent has shown them messages, orders and bank balances that belonged to other accounts, according to a Reuters review of internal posts.

points: Staff reported Muse raising childcare requests, career advice and product orders they had never made.
In one case Muse tacked someone else's Capital One and Charles Schwab balances onto a reply about weather and tides.
Another employee got a reminder to answer her sister on Signal, though she did not recall granting Muse access to other apps.
Meta says employees run different versions of Muse than the public, and that collecting this kind of feedback is the purpose of internal testing.
Muse launched in September and has passed 10 million downloads.

sections.text: An agent with memory and access to a user's other apps has to keep every account's state strictly isolated; these reports show how a context mix-up becomes a privacy breach rather than a mere wrong answer.
